about: Golden vectors for @agent-watch/fingerprint. Every producer (TypeScript poller and source indexer, Python span processor) must reproduce every `expected` exactly. Strings are hashed as UTF-8. Digests are lowercase hex. The package exports the same scheme string as FINGERPRINT_SCHEME; digests from different schemes never compare.

rules.normalise: NFC; replace every CRLF with LF; split on LF; strip trailing whitespace from each line; join with LF; strip trailing whitespace from the end. Never change case. Implementations must strip trailing whitespace in linear time (e.g. a match anchored after a non-whitespace character).
rules.prefixText:
Take the leading run of messages whose role is exactly `system` or `developer`. Message content that is a string is used as is; a list keeps the parts that are objects with `type` "text" and a string `text`, joined with "

" (every other part is ignored); anything else (missing, null, an object, a number) is the empty string. Join the run's contents with "

" and normalise. No leading instruction message: null. Producers shingle a prefix with shingleDigests(prefixText(messages)); joining with anything else changes the shingles (a quote ending one message and a quote starting the next form a concatenation seam across the blank line).
rules.prefixDigest: prefixText(messages); null gives {digest: null, cause: "no_instructions"}; the empty string gives {digest: null, cause: "empty_instructions"}; otherwise {digest: sha256 hex of the text, full 32 bytes, cause: null}.
rules.toolsetDigest: Empty list: null. Each tool's name is `name` if it is a string, else `function.name` if a string, else "". Canonical JSON: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, strings escaped as JSON.stringify does (non-ASCII unescaped; Python json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False)); numbers written as ECMAScript Number::toString writes them (1.0 is "1", 1e21 is "1e+21", 1e-7 is "1e-7", 0.000001 is "0.000001"; integers beyond 2^53 are first read as doubles). Sort tools by (name, canonical JSON) comparing UTF-16 code units, join canonical JSON with "\n", sha256, full 32 bytes.
rules.shingleDigests: tokens(text); every window of 8 consecutive tokens joined by one space; sha256 truncated to the first 16 bytes; deduplicated keeping first occurrence; stop once 512 distinct digests are held. Fewer than 8 tokens: [].
rules.sourceSkipReason: ext (with the dot, compared lowercased) must be one of .py .md .txt .j2 .jinja .yaml .yml .json .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .cjs, else "unsupported_extension" (checked first). A byte length over 1048576 gives "too_large". Otherwise null.
rules.sourceShingleDigests: sourceSkipReason(ext, UTF-8 byte length of fileText); when not null, {digests: [], skipped: that reason}. Otherwise the shingleDigests rule with a cap of 20000 and skipped: null.
rules.rekey: Server side only. HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the tenant key (at least 32 bytes) over the raw bytes of the hex digest (32 or 64 lowercase hex chars), truncated to the first 16 bytes.
rules.sharedShingles: Test helper, not exported: the number of shingleDigests(runtimeText) that also appear in sourceShingleDigests(fileText, ext).digests. Shows the seam rules let a runtime prompt meet the file that built it.
rules.prefixShingles: Test helper, not exported: shingleDigests(prefixText(messages)), or shingleDigests("") when prefixText is null. Locks the join producers must use.
